[p-1a2b3c] nginx.service stopped: blocked by SELinux
Waiting for your decision, found by basalt on 2026-10-04 10:15 UTC

  nginx.service is not running because SELinux blocked something it needs.
  SELinux denied httpd_t the read permission on /srv/site/index.html (labeled
  user_home_t), 3 times. If you apply it, the assistant will add a rule that
  labels /srv/site and everything below it as httpd_sys_content_t (relabeling
  the files already there) and then restart nginx.service.

What will run (exactly these commands, as root, in this order)
  $ semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_content_t '/srv/site(/.*)?'
  $ restorecon -Rv /srv/site
  $ systemctl restart nginx.service

Risk: medium (adds a lasting SELinux rule for /srv/site).
Undo: a snapshot is taken before and after, so you can go back to the state
before the change; a rollback takes effect at the next boot. Note: the labels
of files under /srv are on a separate volume and stay as they are.
  $ sudo basalt snapshots rollback --before p-1a2b3c

Next step
  Apply it:   sudo basalt apply p-1a2b3c
              (without a prompt: sudo basalt apply p-1a2b3c --yes --confirm 2ea96edb)
  Ignore it:  sudo basalt ignore p-1a2b3c

Evidence
  - state: failed/failed, result exit-code, main process exited status 1, restarts 0
